reason: The cited evidence (E2) clearly states that SFE governs deformation mechanisms and mentions the ~40 mJ/m² threshold for TRIP/twinning vs. dislocation glide, supporting the first two premises. However, the specific strength–ductility trade-off predicted in the third premise is not directly supported by the cited passages, and no evidence is provided that SFE differences are the primary driver of property variations among these specific alloy subsets.
premises: SFE governs activation of deformation mechanisms (TRIP, TWIP, dislocation glide) in FCC alloys
SFE below ~40 mJ/m² favors TRIP and deformation twinning; high SFE favors dislocation glide
Lower SFE leads to higher strength and lower ductility; higher SFE leads to higher ductility and lower strength
SFE differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its subsets are the primary cause of mechanical property differences
